badrinath.title: Char Dham yatra registration is compulsory (free)
badrinath.summary: The Uttarakhand portal says you must register yourself and your vehicle before the journey, download a Yatra Registration Letter with a QR code, and verify yourself at each shrine on arrival. It describes registration as free. Helicopter tickets are sold only through IRCTC.
badrinath.cost: Free, according to the official page.

badrinath.title: Vehicle registration, Green Card and Trip Card for Char Dham routes
badrinath.summary: The official transport portal says commercial passenger vehicles (buses, minibuses, taxis) need a Green Card and Trip Card for the Char Dham shrines: ₹400 for up to 10 seats and ₹600 above 10 seats, plus a ₹50 user charge. Private vehicles are asked to register and pay a user charge; no Green Card is mentioned for them.
badrinath.cost: Commercial: ₹400 (up to 10 seats) or ₹600 (over 10 seats) plus ₹50 user charge. Private user-charge amount is not stated.

darjeeling.title: West Bengal homestay registration
darjeeling.summary: We could not find a reliable source on whether North Bengal homestays must be registered, or how guests can verify one. Treat any claim of 'government approved' as unverified until you can see a certificate.

dooars-homestays.title: West Bengal homestay registration
dooars-homestays.summary: We could not find a reliable source on whether North Bengal homestays must be registered, or how guests can verify one. Treat any claim of 'government approved' as unverified until you can see a certificate.

dooars-homestays.title: Jaldapara and Gorumara safari booking rules change often
dooars-homestays.summary: The forest department restored online booking for elephant safaris at Jaldapara and Gorumara in September 2025 and began online booking at Jaldapara again in October 2026. Jeep or car safaris were booked offline at times. Book only through the forest department's official channels or a registered operator.

hanle-changthang-homestays.title: Inner Line Permit for Indian citizens: no longer required
hanle-changthang-homestays.summary: Ladakh's administration removed the Inner Line Permit requirement for Indian nationals in August 2021. Many older blogs still say it is needed. Indian visitors are instead asked for an environment fee receipt (next rule).

hanle-changthang-homestays.title: Protected Area Permit for foreign nationals
hanle-changthang-homestays.summary: Foreign nationals (including OCI and PIO holders per one source) need a Protected Area Permit for inner-line areas, arranged through a registered Leh travel agent. Some Changthang areas, including Hanle, have extra limits for foreigners.
hanle-changthang-homestays.cost: ₹600 per person reported by one source.

hanle-changthang-homestays.title: Ladakh homestay registration
hanle-changthang-homestays.summary: We could not find a reliable current source on whether Ladakh homestays must be registered with the tourism department, or how guests can check it.

hanle-changthang-homestays.title: Taxis and self-drive cars rented outside Ladakh cannot do sightseeing
hanle-changthang-homestays.summary: Under a Ladakh taxi union rule, a taxi or self-drive car hired outside Ladakh (Delhi, Manali, Srinagar, Chandigarh) may bring you to Leh but cannot be used for sightseeing to Nubra, Pangong, Tso Moriri or Hanle. You hire a Leh-registered taxi for those trips.

hanle-changthang-homestays.title: Bikes rented outside Ladakh cannot be used beyond Leh town
hanle-changthang-homestays.summary: A bike rented in Delhi, Manali or Srinagar can enter Leh but riders are turned back from Nubra, Pangong and Hanle circuits. Riders park it and rent a Leh-registered bike (yellow plate) for those days.

hanle-changthang-homestays.title: Your own private vehicle can be driven within Ladakh
hanle-changthang-homestays.summary: Privately owned cars and bikes (white plate) registered in your own name, or reportedly your spouse's or parent's name, are generally allowed to visit Nubra, Pangong and Tso Moriri. Union members at checkpoints may ask for proof of ownership.

hanle-changthang-homestays.title: Environment fee receipt and photo ID for restricted-area circuits
hanle-changthang-homestays.summary: Indian tourists pay an environment fee online through the Leh tourist management portal and show the receipt with a photo ID at checkposts for Nubra Valley, Khardung La, Turtuk, Pangong, Tso Moriri and Hanle. The official page confirms that the fee exists and that it includes environment, Red Cross and wildlife components.
hanle-changthang-homestays.cost: Reported as about ₹450 per person in one 2026 source; another source lists ₹100. The official page we read shows no amount.

jibhi-tirthan-homestays.summary: Himachal Pradesh has made registration of homestays and B&Bs mandatory under its Homestay Rules, 2025, with an online portal launched in February 2026. Guests can ask the host for the registration number.

jibhi-tirthan-homestays.summary: Himachal charges an entry tax at its border barriers for vehicles registered in other states; Himachal-registered vehicles are exempt. singalila-sandakphu-homestays.title: Singalila National Park: entry permit, and a registered guide is required beyond Tumling
singalila-sandakphu-homestays.summary: Trekking to Sandakphu or Phalut means entering Singalila National Park. You buy an entry permit at the Manebhanjan or Dhotrey forest checkpost and hire a state-registered guide (a porter is optional). If you go only as far as Tumling you do not need the park permit.

singalila-sandakphu-homestays.title: West Bengal homestay registration

singalila-sandakphu-homestays.title: Singalila entry fee, camera fee and vehicle fee
singalila-sandakphu-homestays.summary: Sources disagree on the numbers. Indian entry: ₹100 to ₹120 per person (per day inside the park in some sources). Foreigners: ₹200 to ₹500. Vehicle: ₹100 or ₹400. Still camera ₹100; video ₹300 to ₹400.
singalila-sandakphu-homestays.cost: ₹100 to ₹120 per Indian visitor; ₹100 to ₹400 per vehicle.

singalila-sandakphu-homestays.title: Vehicles inside Singalila: time window and monsoon closure
singalila-sandakphu-homestays.summary: One source says cars may enter the park only between 7 am and 2 pm, and another says the park is closed during the monsoon. Both are single-source claims.
